risks: Low for patients if no referral is lost; the main risk is that required fields delay urgent referrals from practices without rapid tests, which the documented exception addresses.
consent: No individual consent: the redesign changes a service process and uses aggregate counts; practices are informed before each change and can comment through the primary care network.
data: Weekly aggregate counts and a de-identified sample for bypass review; no patient identifiers leave the referral system.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: practices without rapid test kits, often rural or in deprived areas, returned the most referrals when a test field was required. Returned referrals are reported by practice group, the exception is monitored, and urgent referrals are never returned without a same-day call to the practice.
effectiveness: Success is fewer returned referrals and a shorter or unchanged time to triage without high bypass or practice burden.
efficiency: Uses the lean coach and existing staff; the template is already built.
costs: No new costs beyond staff time within existing roles.
grants: None needed; the write-up could support a regional application to spread the redesign to other specialties.
partnerships: Triage nurses, booking clerks, two family doctors, the digital health office and a patient partner from the regional patient advisory council.
rebPath: Service improvement using aggregate data; the regional quality office will be asked to confirm that no research ethics review is needed before publication, following the TCPS 2 guidance on quality improvement.
limitations: One intake, overlapping countermeasures, small practice timing sample.
summary: Low-risk service redesign with an urgent-referral safeguard and equity reporting by practice group.
